key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in at most 5(n-1) rounds, giving an essentially linear-time bound in the number of iterations.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens the practical and theoretical cost estimate for graph-isomorphism-related refinement methods that are also used in algebraic, logical, and ML settings.
method: Analyze the refinement process of the classical 2-WL algorithm round by round.
Prove a linear upper bound of 5(n-1) iterations for termination.
Extend the argument to k-WL for k≥3, yielding O(n^(k-1)/(k-2)! + n^(k-2)) rounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new proven worst-case iteration bound, improving the prior O(n log n) upper bound and matching the known Ω(n) lower bound asymptotically.
watch_item: The result bounds the number of refinement rounds, but implementation speed and memory use can still be dominated by per-round costs on large graphs.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
